chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from his father who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'Shall I begin with Al-Medina or with Makkah?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Begin with Makkah and end with Al-Medina, for it is superior'.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended order for performing the main Hajj circumambation according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the preferred ritual sequence for the returning pilgrim (Hajj al-Tamattu' or Qiran) is clarified: one should perform the Tawaf al-Ifadah in Mecca first and then conclude with the visit to Medina. This establishes the spiritual hierarchy where the sanctity of the Kaaba takes precedence in the ritual sequence, yet the finality in Medina signifies the completion of the pilgrimage journey by connecting with the Prophet's legacy. The Imam's directive underscores the merit of ending the sacred journey in the city of the Prophet, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the interconnection of the two holiest sites.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Abdullah, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father who said,
‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Shall I begin with Al-Medina or with Makkah?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Begin with Makkah and end with Al-Medina, for it is superior’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah has narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from his father who has said the following: “
I once asked abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ’Should I commence with al-Madinah or Makkah?’ He (the Imam) replied, ’Commence with Makkah and end with al-Madinah; it is more virtuous.’”
